executive_summary: This chapter introduces statistical thinking, data collection, central tendency measures (arithmetic mean and median), and graphical data representations (dot plots and clustered/double column graphs). The arithmetic mean is conceptualized as a 'fair-share' equalized value, while the median is the middle value of ordered data. The chapter explores how extreme values (outliers) affect the mean significantly while leaving the median relatively stable. It also covers interpreting variability, clusters, gaps, and double-bar graphs for comparative analysis across groups.
key_takeaways: Arithmetic Mean Formula: Mean = (∑ x_i) / N
Median Rule: Middle term of sorted dataset.
Dot Plot: Statistical chart displaying dots stacked above a number line for discrete data.
Clustered Bar Graph: Bar graph displaying multiple bars per category for side-by-side comparison.
